0.0.n: An Okinawan word forming part of the aquarium’s name, 美ら海.

0.1.n: Combines with 美ら to form 美ら海, the name Churaumi, meaning beautiful sea.

0.2.n: Forms part of the full place name 美ら海水族館, Churaumi Aquarium.

0.3.n: Marks the destination reached with 到着する, to arrive.

0.4.n: 到着する becomes 到着しました in the polite past form.

1.0.n: Names the animal being discussed; Japanese does not specify singular or plural here.

1.1.n: Adds the whale shark to the things the speaker found impressive.

1.2.n: Past form of すごい, with い replaced by かった.

1.3.n: Short for の; adds an explanatory tone before です.

1.4.n: Makes the explanatory ん construction polite; the past tense is already expressed by すごかった.

1.5.n: Connects this praise to a contrasting personal reaction in the next line.

2.0.n: Combines with に to describe the speaker’s own perspective.

2.1.n: Turns 個人的 into 個人的に, describing how the speaker views the experience.

2.2.n: Highlights the speaker’s personal perspective, contrasting it with the preceding praise.

2.3.n: Refers to a dark-colored manta ray, not an individual animal’s name.

2.4.n: Marks ブラックマンタ as the animal described by 可愛かったです.

2.5.n: An emphatic, conversational version of とても, strengthening the following description.

2.6.n: 可愛い becomes 可愛かった in the past; です adds politeness.

0.tip: Japanese often leaves out the subject, so no word for we appears here.

1.lit: Whale shark too was amazing, the thing is, but...
1.tip: んですが adds explanatory softness before introducing a contrast.

2.lit: As for personally, the black manta ray really was cute.
2.tip: 個人的には frames the comment as the speaker’s own opinion.
